articles.title: CNCF Research Shows Virtual Machines Remain Central as AI Workloads Evolve
articles.summary: New research from the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) and Linux Foundation Research finds that VMs host an average of 53% of production applications, while emerging AI and agentic workloads a...
articles.description: New research from the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) and Linux Foundation Research finds that VMs host an average of 53% of production applications, while emerging AI and agentic workloads are creating additional demand for virtualisation, particularly where stronger execution isolation is required. By Craig Risi

articles.description: OpenAI has detailed Pando, a new backend that scales Git for concurrent coding-agent workloads without replacing familiar Git workflows. The company reports nearly 80% lower median push latency by coordinating branch updates independently and reusing stored packfiles across fetches. By Eran Stiller

articles.title: Article: Engineering Around Non-Determinism: Evals, Grounding, and Release Gates for AI-Drafted Suspicious Reports
articles.summary: Moving GenAI into high-stakes production requires treating non-determinism as an engineering problem. This architectural blueprint shows engineering leaders and architects how to build trustworthy age...
articles.description: Moving GenAI into high-stakes production requires treating non-determinism as an engineering problem. This architectural blueprint shows engineering leaders and architects how to build trustworthy agentic workflows using knowledge graphs, dual-layer eval judges, CI/CD release gates, and regression testing against golden datasets to automate drafting while maintaining zero-hallucination compliance.

articles.title: QCon San Francisco 2026: Lessons from Building a $100M Product in Six Weeks at OpenAI
articles.summary: At QCon San Francisco 2026, OpenAI's Brian Yang described building the ChatGPT ads product with Codex agents and no human-written code. He outlined layered testing, sandboxes, and batched pull request...
articles.description: At QCon San Francisco 2026, OpenAI's Brian Yang described building the ChatGPT ads product with Codex agents and no human-written code. He outlined layered testing, sandboxes, and batched pull request reviews, and noted failure modes such as code "slop" and unsafe agent actions. He advised gradual adoption and framed engineers as managers of agents. By Daniel Curtis
